No exposed precision-preserving sincos shortcut exists in current cuTile. Inspected NVlabs/cutile-rs commit 2eed75e8f552be31216ddf2019288f03dfec4939.

  • Verified lowering: Rust sin/cos/exp emit separate Tile IR operations. The opcode inventory has no sincos, external-call, or inline-assembly operation.
  • Verified precision: Tile IR 13.3 defaults exp to full, using CUDA Math API; approx is explicitly unsupported for f64. The bytecode writer supplies that full default. sin/cos preserve f64 types and expose no approximation modifier. Their specific ULP bounds and backend implementation are not established by the inspected Tile specification.
  • Verified compiler controls: CompileOptions exposes occupancy/warps and optimization/debug controls; stage two defaults to --opt-level 3. No fast-math switch is exposed. NVCC flags do not directly control this Tile compilation path.
  • Unverified: tileiras might merge separate sin/cos range reduction internally. Neither source nor documentation promises this; inspect generated SASS before assuming duplicate reduction. NVIDIA recommends double-precision sincos in its SIMT API, but using it here requires a different backend or compiler support.

Best immediate experiment: specialize all-real wavevectors once at construction, eliminating the decay dot product and exp in plane.rs. This retains complex128 coefficients and exact f64 trig, removing one transcendental per point×mode. Next try explicit f64 fma(..., NearestEven, Disabled) in accumulation; qualify rounding differences.

No edits, remote operations, builds, or benchmarks performed.

No concrete lowering blocker found.

  • Scalar bool is supported end to end: bool → i1, bool implements DType, and scalar arguments use that trait. Existing GPU control-flow tests pass both true and false to exactly this kind of scalar conditional.
  • Your FMA modifiers are correct: f64 supports NearestEven; f64 does not support enabled FTZ. ftz::Disabled omits that attribute in the Rust wrapper. full is an exponential mode, not a supported FMA mode; retain NearestEven. FMA specification.
  • sm89 is supported, including f64, by Tile IR 13.3’s architecture/type tables. No RTX4080-specific restriction found.

One performance qualification: the runtime bool branch is supported, but source inspection cannot establish whether tileiras actually avoids/speculates exp. Parent timing or disassembly must establish that.

Credible baseline, with one useful stronger comparator.

  • matmul detects one output column and dispatches directly to matvec_colmajor. Its inner loop uses SIMD complex multiply-add, not generic GEMM or scalar nalgebra.
  • Native treams enables faer’s Rayon feature. get_global_parallelism() defaults to the current Rayon pool size. Run separate processes with explicit RAYON_NUM_THREADS; log the actual pool size.
  • Potential weakness: parallel column-major matvec partitions columns, allocates M × threads temporary complex values, then sums partial outputs serially. At 16 threads, that is 12 MiB / 24 MiB scratch per call for the proposed shapes.
  • Row-major matvec instead uses SIMD row dots and partitions output rows, avoiding that temporary.

Narrow comparison: retain the existing column-major baseline; additionally prepack fixed F once into row-major storage and invoke the same faer API. Compare 1/8/16/32 threads and report the fastest CPU configuration. Exclude one-time CPU packing and GPU upload equally from steady-state timings, recording both setup costs separately. This tests a concrete baseline weakness without adding another library.

No edits or benchmarks performed.

No actionable correctness findings in the requested plane-kernel change.

  • Six accumulators implement the correct complex product signs for each component; concatenation preserves [x, y, z, padding].
  • The real-wavevector shortcut checks every imaginary component for exact zero. Shared polarization validation rejects nonfinite wavevectors before that decision.
  • Point indexing, padded layout, and [128,4] output partitioning remain consistent. Existing boundary cases exercise 127/128/129/257 points.
  • Every changed arithmetic operation remains f64 with nearest-even FMA and FTZ disabled. FMA changes rounding, which the cancellation test meaningfully exercises.

Limits: source review only; no builds or hardware execution. The long-path test verifies attenuation/intensity, so it does not independently qualify phase accuracy at phase magnitude 1e12. That is an existing transcendental qualification boundary, not a demonstrated regression.
